abstract: Aortic and vena caval reconstruction associated with tumor resection is very rare. We describe a 22-year-old man with a retroperitoneal metastasis from a germ-cell tumor previously treated with chemotherapy who presented with a huge mass involving the infrarenal aorta and the inferior vena cava. He underwent retroperitoneal lymph node dissection with concomitant aortic and caval reconstruction that included customization of a new caval bifurcation. His postoperative recovery was uneventful, and he remained well 36 months after the operation. Complementary follow-up imaging examinations demonstrated that the aortic and venous interposition grafts were patent and that there was no local or distant disease recurrence.
abstract_ja: 大動脈および下大静脈の再建を腫瘍切除に伴って行う症例は極めてまれです。化学療法を受けた既往のある胚細胞腫瘍の後腹膜転移により、腎動脈下部の大動脈および下大静脈を巻き込む巨大な腫瘤を呈した22歳男性を報告します。後腹膜リンパ節郭清と大動脈・下大静脈の同時再建を行い、新たな下大静脈分岐を形成しました。術後経過は良好でした。追加のフォローアップ画像検査では、大動脈および静脈の人工血管介在移植片は開存しており、局所または遠隔の再発は認められませんでした。36か月間良好な状態を保っています。
